root_idea.summary: The root centers on water or a tear, especially fluid issuing from the eye.
root_idea.development: The basic image of eye-fluid extends to shedding tears, flowing or exuding moisture and other liquids, and several tear-related anatomical and figurative expressions.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Classical Arabic noun دَمْعٌ rather than the inflected internal QAC lemma form.

senses.definition: Tears; the fluid issuing from the eye.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quran, the noun occurs in expressions describing tears flowing from the eyes; one occurrence explicitly connects the tears with grief.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of the eye: to shed tears or have tears flow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The verb is attested with variant imperfect and verbal-noun patterns.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a wound: to ooze or flow blood, like tears.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Descriptions differ over whether the term denotes slight oozing in drops or a more substantial flow; the expression is applied especially to a head wound.

other_classical_meanings.headword_arabic: دَمَعَتِ الجَفْنَةُ / دُمُوعُ الجَفْنَةِ / قَدَحٌ دَمْعَانٌ / جَفْنَةٌ دَامِعَةٌ
other_classical_meanings.definition: To flow or overflow, or to be full to overflowing, of a bowl or vessel; the flowing contents may be grease or gravy.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The same flowing metaphor is also used for liquid issuing from a dyer's strainer and for a vessel whose contents overflow from its sides.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The liquid flowing from a dyer's strainer.
In poetic usage, for the sun to 'weep': its fierce rays and fine airborne moisture stream forth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a reported figurative interpretation of a poetic expression, not a Quranic citation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The vehement flowing of tears from the eye.
To fill a bowl or vessel so as to make it overflow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a causative Form IV usage applied to a container.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To shed tears or weep.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The attestation is explicitly reported as possibly post-classical.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To draw forth tears.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The evidence presents this as an apparent or qualified Form X usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A single tear or drop of eye-fluid.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the unit form of دَمْعٌ, distinct from the collective or mass sense ‘tears.’

other_classical_meanings.definition: A known medicinal substance called ‘David’s tears.’
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression is a conventional name for a medicine, not ordinary eye-fluid.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Rain or moisture flowing from clouds; a day characterized by fine drizzle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The cloud expression is figurative, modeled on tears flowing from the eye.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Wine, figuratively called ‘the tear of the vine.’
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is an idiomatic designation rather than a literal description of eye-fluid.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The fluid flowing from a grapevine in spring.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This refers to vine exudate or sap, distinct from the idiomatic use of دَمْعُ الكَرْمِ for wine.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Tearful; quick to shed tears or weep; of an eye, shedding many tears.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The descriptions apply to persons or eyes without imposing a general gender restriction; some forms are adjectives and one is the active participle of دَمَعَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A mark made with a hot iron on a camel in the area where tears run.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The mark is a specialized camel-branding term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Fluid from the eye associated with disease or old age, distinguished by one report from tears; alternatively, traces of tears left on the face.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The evidence preserves two reported interpretations of the same lexical item.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A hot-iron mark made along the eye-edge vein toward the nostril or nostrils.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The mark may occur singly or in pairs; the precise anatomical location is reported with some variation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Earth or soil from which moisture exudes, or that appears ready to exude moisture.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a figurative extension from tears or flowing water to damp soil.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The channel or area where tears run or collect at the sides of the eye; in the plural, the inner and outer angles of the eyes.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural may also denote waters dripping from a mountain side or flowings of tears.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Waters that drop or drip from the side of a mountain; also flowings of tears.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a figurative plural use related to channels or streams of flowing moisture.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A camel bearing the hot-iron mark called دُمُعٌ.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term denotes the marked animal, not the branding mark itself.

cautions: The terminology for a bleeding head wound varies in the cited authorities, especially concerning whether دَامِعَةٌ denotes slight oozing or more substantial bleeding.
The definition of دُمَاعٌ includes alternative reports distinguishing diseased-eye discharge from tears or identifying it as traces left on the face.
The Form V entry تَدَمَّعَ is explicitly qualified in the evidence as possibly post-classical.
